target_customer: Robotics labs needing training and evaluation data, and construction or industrial teams needing 3D models from scans
problem: Robot training data collected by humans is slow and expensive, and scans of buildings are hard to turn into editable models. Moving Atoms builds a physics world model (Atom 1) and scan-to-3D conversion for simulation.
business_model: Services and software: delivered models and simulation environments, policy evaluation
product_category: World models and 3D scan conversion for robotics

founders.name: Shehryar Saroya
founders.background_notes: Company site says the founders are brothers and co-CEOs.

founders.name: Ahmad Saroya
education: University of Oxford, mathematics, left in second year
founders.background_notes: British Mathematical Olympiad gold medalist per the YC page; shipped VR games to the Meta Quest store per the company site.

technical_complexity.rationale: Action-conditioned video world models that respect physics are research-grade, and the company claims a top Physics-IQ score (company claim, unverified).

defensibility.rationale: A two-person team with company-reported benchmark results, facing Nvidia, DeepMind and others working on world models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large players ship world models and scan-to-BIM tools; no acquisition of Moving Atoms is known.

market_need_then: Robot labs lack training data in hard-to-replicate environments, and scan-to-BIM remains manual work. The company says delivery takes 48 hours with 98.7% within 25 mm accuracy, which is its own claim.

identity.logo: A logo image exists but sources do not describe it
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and practical with light humor

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name tied to the physical world, but searches for it return unrelated Atoms companies, including Kalanick's Atoms, and no community or press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Moving Atoms is a Summer 2026 company of two Oxford mathematician brothers combining a world model with scan-to-3D services. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs about this company were found. Outcome is open; the main uncertainties are whether its benchmark claims hold up and whether it can sell against much larger world model efforts.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round with no investors, seen on one aggregator, so it is unverified. The site lists Y Combinator, NVIDIA Inception and OpenAI as backers without amounts. Scan-to-BIM tools such as Autodesk ReCap exist but the sources found were undated, so the competitor list is empty. Search results about Atoms (Kalanick) are a different company.
